fixes.explanation: Opposite, friend. Paul says, “When we are vilified, we bless…” So when insults come at the apostles, they answer with a blessing, not a curse. Cursing back is the easy move, and it's not the one Paul names.

Famous is a fun guess, friend, but it's not in the verse. Paul says stewards must be found faithful. Fame is exactly what you'd chase if you were picking a favorite teacher, and Paul doesn't ask for it. He asks for faithful, not a fan club.

Clever sounds right, baker, but that's not what Paul says. The verse says it is required of stewards that they be found faithful. Being clever might get you a few compliments, but it's not the requirement here. Faithful is.

That one isn't in the verse, friend. Paul says the lesson is “…not to go beyond what is written.” Signs and wonders would be the fireworks show, but Paul points the Corinthians back to what is written. His lesson is the plain page, not a show.
Comfort doesn't fit here, baker. Paul says, “Then you will not take pride in one man over another.” Comfort is a warm word, but it's not the one in the verse. So the word is pride.

That's his point, baker. Paul asks, “What do you have that you did not receive?” Then he asks, “And if you did receive it, why do you boast as though you did not?” Everything they have came to them as a gift, so boasting as though it didn't doesn't fit.

False is right, baker. Paul asks, “And if you did receive it, why do you boast as though you did not?” He's questioning boasting as though what they have was never received. I've learned to say "thank you" before "look at me."

That's the wish, baker. Paul says, “How I wish you really were kings, so that we might be kings with you!” Just before it, he says, “Without us, you have become kings.” And if it were really true, he'd get to be a king right alongside them.

Paul says the opposite, friend. He writes, “I am not writing this to shame you, but to warn you as my beloved children.” His stated purpose is to warn them as his beloved children. A warning to beloved children is a different thing from shaming them.

No gift in this verse, baker. Paul says Timothy “…will remind you of my way of life in Christ Jesus…” Timothy is coming with a reminder, not with an offering plate. His job is to bring Paul's way of life back to their minds.

True, baker. Paul says, “But I will come to you shortly, if the Lord is willing…” He's sending Timothy, and he plans to come himself, if the Lord is willing. Just before that he says, “Some of you have become arrogant, as if I were not coming to you.” (1 Corinthians 4:18)

Not that one, baker. Paul says he'll find out “…not only what these arrogant people are saying, but what power they have.” Then he adds, “For the kingdom of God is not a matter of talk but of power.” So he's looking past the talk to the power. Who taught them first isn't what he's after.
